newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady-$1.50 per cwt higher, with strength tied to heat- and humidity-related reductions in marketings, livestock dealers said.

However, several packer buyers in the central Iowa/southern Minnesota area said they were able to buy enough hogs late Monday to ship overnight. Steep price advances during the day on Monday encouraged farmers to market a few extra hogs late, they said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota sales were light at a steady $60.00-$60.50 in the country and $61.00-$61.50 plants.
Illinois hogs sold $1.00-$1.50 higher at $60.00-$61.50 in the country and $61.50-$62.00 at plants, with several plants reportedly paying higher for premium quality hogs.
Gains in Illinois were fortified by tight marketings amid the heat and high humidity, sources there said.
"I don't think we're going to have much going on, its too hot," one Illinois buyer said.

Indiana hogs sold steady at $59.00 to $60.00, with a few at $61.00 in the country and up to $61.50 at plants. Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $59.00 to $60.00 in the country and $61.50 to $62.00, possibly $62.50 at plants.
